title: Normalize timeout behavior across Node runtimes (undici/fetch) + docs + regression tests
author: Dana Lo
release_notes: - TypeScript SDK: Timeout defaults and error mapping are now consistent across Node runtimes (undici-backed fetch vs. custom dispatcher). Per-request overrides behave the same across environments.
body: Context: As part of the SDK parity audit, we found the TS SDK had materially different timeout behavior depending on runtime: (1) Node 18+ using global fetch (undici) behaved like an overall wall-clock timeout only (and sometimes would not reliably abort mid-response), while (2) environments using our explicit undici dispatcher path would honor connect/read timeouts differently. This inconsistency is showing up as “hung requests” vs. early aborts, and makes it hard for SRE to reason about client-side timeouts across customers. Goals: (a) define a single timeout model in the TS SDK that matches the cross-SDK timeout spec, (b) implement it in a runtime-agnostic way (global fetch / undici dispatcher), (c) map all timeout exits to the same error shape/messages, and (d) add regression tests so this doesn’t drift again. What changed (behavior): We now treat timeouts as three explicit phases where the runtime supports it: connect timeout (time to establish connection / TLS handshake), read timeout (time waiting for the next byte once response started; streaming uses a different default), and overall timeout (wall-clock cap for the request). In runtimes where connect/read can’t be separated, we still enforce overall, and we surface the timeout as overall to avoid pretending we can classify it precisely. Implementation notes: We added a single internal helper that produces a unified AbortSignal for overall timeout and optionally wires an undici Dispatcher with connectTimeout. For read timeout, we implement a timer that resets on body progress for non-streaming responses; for streaming responses we do not enforce read timeout by default (to avoid aborting long-lived streams), but the caller can set it explicitly. Error mapping: All timeout aborts now throw RedwoodTimeoutError with fields: { message, phase: 'connect' | 'read' | 'overall', timeoutMs, requestId? }. We also ensure AbortError from fetch/undici is normalized (no raw DOMException leaking through). Defaults (documented): Non-streaming endpoints default to connect=10s, read=60s, overall=90s. Streaming endpoints default to connect=10s, overall=0 (disabled), read=0 (disabled). These defaults match the direction in the timeouts standard draft and SRE guidance (avoid terminating streaming by default; encourage app-level overall cap if desired). Docs: Updated the TS README + API reference sections to explicitly call out the three timeouts, the streaming defaults, and how timeouts interact with AbortController. Added a troubleshooting note: “If you see RedwoodTimeoutError(phase=overall) on Node 18+ global fetch, you may be behind a proxy buffering the response; prefer streaming + higher overall cap.” Tests: Added regression coverage using undici MockAgent for dispatcher mode and a separate suite that uses the global fetch path (skipped when not available) to ensure: (1) overall timeout aborts, (2) connect timeout triggers when the server doesn’t accept connections, (3) read timeout triggers for stalled bodies on non-streaming, (4) streaming does not time out by default, and (5) error normalization is stable (message + phase + name). Rollout/compat: This should be non-breaking for callers who didn’t set timeouts explicitly, but it may change when/where a timeout triggers for some Node 18+ customers (previously could hang until socket-level timeouts). I think that’s a net improvement and aligns with the parity goals. Checklist: [x] Matches cross-SDK spec direction for streaming vs non-streaming defaults, [x] No secrets logged, [x] Tests cover both runtime paths, [x] Docs updated with examples and migration notes, [x] Verified no retry interaction changes in this PR (retries handled in #287).
commits: sdk(ts): introduce unified timeout model (connect/read/overall) and normalize AbortError mapping
sdk(ts): add undici dispatcher wiring for connect timeout; ensure consistent behavior with global fetch
sdk(ts): add read-timeout enforcement for non-streaming responses (progress-based timer)
docs(ts): document timeout defaults + streaming behavior and AbortController interaction
tests(ts): add MockAgent-based regression tests for connect/read/overall timeouts across runtime paths
chore(ts): refactor request pipeline to share timeout plumbing (no API surface change)
changed_areas: src/resources/chat.ts + src/resources/completions.ts (plumb streaming vs non-streaming defaults)
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan: Can we ensure streaming doesn’t accidentally inherit read timeout from non-streaming? We’ve had customers with 10+ minute streams. Also please align naming with the spec (connect/read/overall) and avoid “requestTimeout” ambiguous wording.

Dana Lo (author): Updated defaults so streaming sets read=0/overall=0 unless user overrides. Also renamed internal options and surfaced docs with connect/read/overall terminology. Added a test asserting streaming does not time out by default.

Rafael Mendes: +1 on not timing out streaming by default. For non-streaming, please confirm the read timer resets on chunked transfer progress (so we don’t kill large responses). Also ensure jitter/backoff retries aren’t triggered on client abort.

Dana Lo (author): Read timer resets on each body chunk; added a unit test with a slow-chunk response. This PR doesn’t touch retry classification; aborts still surface as RedwoodTimeoutError and are not classified retryable.
Ethan Park: From gateway side, request-id header is sometimes only available once headers are received. Do we attach requestId to timeout errors when it exists? (connect timeout won’t have it.)
Dana Lo (author): Yes—if headers are received and we’ve captured x-request-id, RedwoodTimeoutError will include it. Connect timeout won’t have requestId; test added for both cases.
Elliot Price: Docs request: please add a short snippet showing per-request override and note that AbortController cancels immediately regardless of timeout settings.
Dana Lo (author): Added snippet and clarified precedence: explicit AbortSignal abort wins; timeout signal is composed.
Leila Farouk: Tests look good. One concern: global fetch tests may be flaky in CI when network is involved—are we fully mocking?
Dana Lo (author): Fully mocked using local http server + deterministic timers; no external network. Marked the global-fetch suite to skip when fetch isn’t available.
Ibrahim Khan: Approving. This unblocks the conformance harness work; please link this in ENG-2487.
